tools.name: explain_transaction
tools.description: Explain one Sui transaction in plain English: what happened, the steps, who gained or lost which coins (with USD), the fee and the status. Use it whenever you have a transaction digest. Example: { digest: "5ajkuHAnivMiKRne6EYS2bzvHpCHWYx849cmoSHN89Vm" }.

tools.name: wallet_profile
tools.description: Everything about a wallet in one call: total value with price status, top coins, DeFi and launchpad positions, SuiNS names and labels, who first funded it, its trading record and its latest transactions. Use it first for any question about an address or a .sui name. Example: { address: "example.sui"

tools.name: wallet_history
tools.description: A wallet's transactions since genesis, newest first, each as one decoded sentence with the coins in and out. Filter by coin, direction (in or out) and days. Page with cursor. Spam airdrops are left out. Example: { address: "0x...", limit: 10 }.

tools.name: balance_at
tools.description: The exact balance a wallet held at a past time or checkpoint, read from full history. With coin, that coin's balance and the transaction that last changed it. Without coin, every coin it held then, valued at that time's prices. Example: { address: "example.sui", coin: "SUI", time: "2025-06-01T00:00:

tools.name: token_info
tools.description: A coin's price, market cap, liquidity, volume and holder count, its safety checks (mint authority, deny list, concentration), its top 10 holders with linked-wallet clusters, and a report on its creator's past launches. Use it to judge a coin. Example: { coin: "DEEP" }.

tools.name: trace_funds
tools.description: Follow money between addresses. direction in: who sent funds to this address, hop by hop back, plus who first funded it. out: where its funds went, hop by hop forward. both: its largest counterparties either way. Exchanges and protocols end a path. Returns the 15 largest flows. Example: { address: "

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find anything on Sui by text: coins by symbol or name, SuiNS names, perps markets, pools, packages, addresses, objects and digests. Returns ids to pass to the other tools. Example: { query: "deep" }.

tools.name: price
tools.description: USD prices for up to 50 coins, now or at a past time. Pass coin types or symbols. Example: { coins: ["SUI", "DEEP"] }.

tools.name: sql
tools.description: Run one SQL SELECT over every Sui transaction, event, object version and balance change since genesis. Needs an API key. Returns up to 100 rows; page with execution_id and offset. If it is still running, call again with execution_id. Tables and columns: https://api.tide.ad/v1/sql/schema. Example: {

tools.name: explain_unsigned
tools.description: Check a Sui transaction before signing it: tide simulates it, explains what it would do in plain words, and checks every recipient, coin and package against full history. Returns safe, caution or danger with findings and evidence links. Block on danger. Pass tx_bytes (base64 TransactionData, or Tran

tools.name: get_object
tools.description: Read any Sui object by id: type, owner, version and fields, with its recent change history (which transactions changed it). Example: { id: "0x..." }.

tools.name: get_object_at
tools.description: Read a Sui object as it was at a version, checkpoint or time: its fields and owner then, or whether it was deleted or wrapped. Use it for what a pool, vault or position looked like before a change. Example: { id: "0x...", time: "2026-10-30T00:00:00Z" }.

tools.name: object_children
tools.description: List the dynamic fields of an object with decoded names and values (tables, bags, kiosks, pools, registries), or with depth 1 to 3, its tree of children. Page with cursor. Example: { id: "0x..." }.

tools.name: package_info
tools.description: A Move package. With only id: its modules, functions and upgrade history. With module and function: how to call it, each parameter explained, with a TypeScript snippet. With window (24h, 7d or 30d): calls per day and per function, failures and top callers. Example: { id: "0x2", module: "coin", funct

tools.name: events
tools.description: List on-chain events by Move event type or by package, newest first, with an optional time or checkpoint range. Page with cursor. Example: { type: "0x...::pool::SwapEvent", limit: 10 }.

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description: One checkpoint by sequence number, or the newest with seq "latest": time, epoch, gas totals and its transactions as one-line sentences. Use it to see what is happening on chain right now. Example: { seq: "latest" }.

tools.name: candles
tools.description: OHLCV price candles for a coin, in USD. Pick interval and an optional from and to. Example: { coin: "SUI", interval: "1h" }.

tools.name: nfts
tools.description: The NFTs and kiosk items an address owns: name, collection, image and listing state. Page with cursor. Example: { address: "example.sui" }.

tools.name: staking
tools.description: With address: the wallet's staked SUI, per stake its validator, principal, rewards and status. With validator: that validator's stake, commission and APY per epoch. Example: { address: "example.sui" }.

tools.name: order_book
tools.description: DeepBook order books. With nothing: every pool with best bid, ask and 24h volume. With pool: its depth and latest trades. With address: the wallet's open orders and recent fills. Example: { pool: "0x..." }.

tools.name: address_kind
tools.description: Tell what an address is: a plain key (ed25519, secp256k1, secp256r1), a passkey, a zkLogin address (with its provider), a multisig (members and threshold), an object, a package, or an address that never signed. Example: { address: "0x..." }.

tools.name: docs
tools.description: Search the tide API docs for the method that answers a question, with its parameters, credits and a curl example. Use it when no other tool fits; then call the method over REST at https://api.tide.ad. Example: { question: "transfers of a coin between two times" }.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
